tools: Writing a list and picking one thing [self] used 2

moments.text: You had too many things at once, work launch, a sick kid, and moving flat.
You noticed you cried in the car.
You wrote a list and picked one thing for the day.
You felt slightly lighter.
You asked your partner to take the school runs this week.
You took a five minute walk before answering emails.
You said no to a new committee at work, and it felt good.
You apologised to your kids later.
You picked one thing again, finished it, and stopped there.
You took a five minute walk before a hard meeting.
You asked a friend to help pack boxes.
Your friend came with pizza.
You handled the move, and felt proud of how you handled it.
You noticed you felt exhausted after the move.
You noticed overwhelm starts when you try to do everything perfectly.
You left some laundry undone on purpose and rested instead.
You took a five minute walk after a fight with your manager.
You did one thing a day, and today it was the tax form.
You asked for an extension on a deadline, and got it.
You read a book in the sun.
You noticed you now ask for help sooner.
You wrote the list and picked one thing.
You turned down a second project and felt no guilt this time.
You noticed you felt steadier than in spring.

skills_full.name: Picking one thing
skills_full.in_your_words: When everything piles up, you write a list and choose one thing for the day. You keep it small, finish that, and stop there.

skills_full.name: Asking for help
skills_full.in_your_words: You ask your partner, your friend, or work for help when there is too much on your plate. You let other people take some of the load.

skills_full.name: Taking a short walk
skills_full.in_your_words: You take a five minute walk before a hard moment, like emails or a meeting. It helps you come back a bit steadier.

skills_full.name: Noticing perfection pressure
skills_full.in_your_words: You notice overwhelm can start when you try to do everything perfectly. That gives you a clearer sign of what is setting it off.

skills_full.name: Picking one thing
skills_full.in_your_words: You choose one thing for the day, finish it, and leave the rest. That can help you feel lighter and keep some space for rest.

skills_full.name: Leaving some undone
skills_full.in_your_words: You leave some laundry undone on purpose and rest instead. You give yourself permission to stop without guilt.

skills_full.name: Noticing when you feel lighter
skills_full.in_your_words: You notice the small shift when you slow down, like feeling slightly lighter or asking for help sooner. That helps you see what calms things down.

skills_full.name: Enjoying a small pause
skills_full.in_your_words: You make room for a quiet bit of calm, like reading a book in the sun. It is a small moment that helps you settle.

skills_full.name: Noticing when you feel steadier
skills_full.in_your_words: You notice when you feel steadier than before, and you can see that lighter feeling in everyday life. You also notice when asking for help sooner is part of that shift.

skills_full.name: Noticing the exhausted feeling
skills_full.in_your_words: You notice when overwhelm shows up as feeling exhausted, like after the move. That helps you spot what is happening before you try to do everything perfectly.
